mechanism: The history page eagerly creates every row and repeatedly decodes each stored JSON string. The revised fix uses a lazy list and caches decoded entries by their exact stored string. This case evaluates the combined reduction in eager row construction and repeated decoding; it does not attribute the full performance gain to JSON parsing alone.
fix_summary: Build history rows on demand, reuse decoded song objects, preserve newest-first order, and delete using the exact original storage key. Keep normal song navigation and the complete remaining history.

performance_oracle.definition: Sampled retired-instruction period sum (hw-instructions) attributed to the app process in the complete externally driven measured window.
performance_oracle.comparison: unfixed >= 1.3 * fixed over >= 3 rounds per variant
performance_oracle.workload_notes: Combined lazy row construction and cached decoding, not isolated JSON parsing. Identical 1,000-song native histories and normal UI workload. Three pairs must each meet 1.3x.
